properties.description:

but no additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hawarden and Alcester.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Elko, NV; Eureka, NV; Lander, NV; Nye, NV; White Pine, NV
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 12:13AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
ESFLKN

A low pressure system over the Pacific Northwest will drop southward
into Northern California Sunday. This storm system will draw abundant
atmospheric moisture associated with Tropical Storm Rachel northward
into Eastern Nevada, resulting in the likelihood of rain Sunday and
Sunday night. Slow storm motions and/or training cells may produce
heavy rainfall and localized flooding.

Of particular concern are recent, large burn scars, including the
Ward fire south of Ely and the Oxley fire north of Wells. Numerous
smaller burn scare from this fire season also remain vulnerable to
flash flooding and debris flow.

Residents near burn scars should have multiple ways to receive Flash
Flood Warning and be prepared to act quickly. Travelers and
recreationists should also remain alert and consider alternate plans.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 8 at 11:59PM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions
with heat index values up to 100. For the Wind Advisory, south
winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Death Valley National Park.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT Friday. For the
Wind Advisory, from 2 PM Saturday to 5 AM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Heat
related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat and
high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These

them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 9 at 1:50AM CDT until October 10 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to
7 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM CDT Saturday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation will occur near high tide
cycles each afternoon.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

cycles each afternoon.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Georgia, including the following areas, Berrien, Lanier and

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

the area. Widespread totals of 4 to 8 inches are expected with
localized amounts of 10 to 15 inches. Given saturated soils from

flash flooding is possible where bands of heavy rain move
repeatedly over the same area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
